title: Deep learning controls electrical stimulation patterns in human visual cortex
summary: The Neuron abstract reports a deep-learning framework trained on trial-resolved recordings from a bidirectional human visual-cortex implant. A learned inverse network and gradient-based optimizer shaped stimulation-evoked population activity, achieved targets at lower currents and elicited more consistent perception than conventional methods. This is an experimental neural-control result, not evidence of restored functional sight. The paper was first published online on 2026-08-07; review here is limited to its abstract and metadata.
ai_technology: Deep learning inverse network and gradient-based optimizer for neural stimulation
organization: University of Zurich; ETH Zurich; University of California, Santa Barbara; Miguel Hernández University

evidence.tested: Within-study human visual-cortex stimulation experiments comparing two learned control approaches with conventional methods; lower currents and more consistent reported percepts.
evidence.unknown: Complete abstract and metadata reviewed. Participant count, implant duration, long-term performance and functional-vision outcomes were not assessed; full-text XML retrieval returned HTTP 500.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained on trial-resolved neural recordings to synthesize and optimize stimulation patterns.
